html:
The Kalina, or Kariña, are a Carib-speaking people of the northern coast of South America, from eastern Venezuela through Guyana and Suriname to French Guiana. The Spanish word "Carib", and through it the name of the Caribbean Sea, comes from their name.

In 1492 they held much of the coast and the lower Orinoco, trading and raiding by canoe. Spanish writers, beginning with Columbus, linked Carib peoples, including the Kalinago of the islands, with cannibalism, and the Spanish crown allowed them to be enslaved. The Kalina fought Spanish missions and allied at times with the Dutch, who settled the Guianas.

Over centuries they lost the coast to plantations, but they survive in all four countries. Their neighbours included the Arawak-speaking Lokono and, inland, the Pemón.
